title: aorch task plan
description: The decomposition contract. The host model decomposes a request and writes this document; aorch validates it and dispatches every task in it. This file is a contract document printed by `aorch decompose --print-schema` — validation itself is hand-rolled in src/decompose.js because this package has no runtime dependencies.

objective.description: The user's request, verbatim. Kept so a reader can judge whether the decomposition preserved the goal.

decomposed.description: false means the request runs as one task and `tasks` must hold exactly one entry. Prefer false when splitting would not let a reviewer approve one part and reject another.

tasks.description: Executed in declared order. Dispatch stops at the first failure.

id.description: Path-safe and unique within the plan; it names the run directory.

kind.description: Routing input, e.g. implementation, testing, documentation, debugging, architecture, security, exploration, research, writing.

agentRole.description: Selects the role agent and derives the routing role. worker: build it. reviewer: judge it without touching it. fixer: repair a task whose verification failed. researcher: find candidates on the web and record URL, license, recency and activity as evidence. analyst: read a named repository and separate what can be borrowed from what cannot. license-reviewer: check the licence text and state what obligations each form of reuse carries. ponytail: look for what does not need to be written at all, and justify whatever survives. writer: draft prose for a bounded chapter or page set at top-tier routing. editor: directly fix wording, phrasing and typos only, and report substance or structure concerns as judgements instead of edits. qa-analyst: read what the QA commands already computed and render a verdict, opening only changed or machine-flagged pages. invest-analyst: analyse evidence someone else gathered into support, refutation and blind spots shaped as decision-record input, never gathering, ranking or ordering trades. refactorer: perform behavior-preserving restructuring only, reporting any public-API or behavior change as a judgement instead of making it. paper-researcher: search academic sources through the paper-search MCP and record bibliographic records, citation counts and the tool each fact came from, never ranking or synthesising. Scouting our own repository is deliberately absent — that reconnaissance stays with the lead, because verifying a delegated survey costs about as much as running it. Web research is the exception researcher covers: a URL and a licence can be re-checked mechanically, so the spot check is cheap.

agentId.description: Optional exact inventory agent ID. Overrides the native preset while agentRole still determines routing role and the task's safety envelope.

role.description: Forbidden in a plan. aorch derives the routing role from agentRole; writing it by hand would let the two disagree.

complexity.description: Optional; derived from risk when absent.

verificationCommands.description: aorch runs these itself after the worker returns and escalates the model ladder on failure. A task without them gets no gate.

allowedProviders.description: Leave unset so both subscriptions compete. Restrict only for a concrete capability reason.

allowedProfileIds.description: Pin the task to named catalogue profiles. Leave unset so the router chooses by evidence; set it only when the task exists to obtain a specific model's judgement, such as the model-upgrade audit.
